info.title: meertrack API
info.summary: Read-only HTTP API for programmatic access to meertrack competitor data.
info.description:
Machine-readable contract for the meertrack v1 API. Use it to
generate clients, import into Postman/Stoplight, or validate requests
and responses.

Auth: every request must include `Authorization: Bearer mt_live_…`.
Keys are minted in the app at Settings → API Keys (admin only).

Rate limit: 60 requests per minute, per workspace, **per serverless
instance**. The limiter is in-process - there is no shared Redis. In
practice this means:
- The `X-RateLimit-Remaining` header reflects the counter on the
  instance that served the current request only. Successive requests
  may be routed to different instances, so the value is not monotonic.
- A burst across multiple cold instances can briefly exceed 60 rpm in
  aggregate. Don't design clients that rely on exactly-60 enforcement.
- Treat 429 + `X-RateLimit-Reset` as the authoritative backoff signal
  and apply jitter; do not extrapolate from `X-RateLimit-Remaining`.

Every successful response and every rate-limited response carries the
`X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, and `X-RateLimit-Reset`
headers. 401 responses carry `WWW-Authenticate` instead.

Parameter validation is strict. On the filtering endpoints
(`/competitors`, `/activity`, `/activity/items`, `/digests`) an
unrecognized query parameter returns `400 unknown_parameter` naming
the offending parameter, and an out-of-range value returns
`400 invalid_parameter` - neither is ignored. Comma-separated
parameters may also be repeated (`?id=A&id=B` is equivalent to
`?id=A,B`); repeating a non-list parameter is an error.

Versioning & deprecation: this is `v1`. Backwards-incompatible
changes ship as `v2` at a new path prefix; `v1` will continue to be
served. One exception, effective 1.1.0: the strict parameter
validation described above was introduced on `v1` rather than held
for `v2`, because the previous behavior returned `200` with
unfiltered data for a request the server had not understood - a
silently wrong answer we judged worse than a breaking change.
Field-level deprecations are announced on a deprecated field via an
`x-deprecated` extension and a `Deprecation: true` header on
affected responses, with at least 90 days' notice before removal;
deprecated *parameters* are marked `deprecated: true` in this
document and echoed in an `X-Meertrack-Deprecated-Parameter`
response header. Subscribe to changes by watching the `info.version`
field in this document - the patch version bumps for additive
changes, the minor version for backwards-compatible behavior
changes.

Questions or access requests: [contact us](https://meertrack.com/contact).

get.description: Returns the caller's auth context (`auth_type`, `subject`), the API key in use (`null` for OAuth callers, which have no API-key record), and the workspace it belongs to.

Returns every competitor tracked by the authenticated workspace. Use
`active` to filter by status, `id` (comma-separated) to restrict to
specific competitors, and `expand=full` to get the full per-competitor
profile (social links, page URLs) instead of the summary shape.

parameters.name: active
parameters.description:
`true` returns active competitors only. `false` returns deactivated
competitors only. Omit to return both.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description:
Restrict the response to the listed competitor UUIDs. Comma-separated,
e.g. `?id=A,B,C`; repeating the key (`?id=A&id=B`) is also accepted and
merges into the same list. Any `id` value that doesn't belong to your
workspace yields `403 forbidden_competitor`. Unlike `/activity`,
inactive competitors are allowed here - `/competitors` is the one
endpoint where deactivated competitors are expected to be visible.

parameters.name: ids
parameters.description: Deprecated alias for `id`. Supply one spelling or the other, not both.

parameters.name: expand
parameters.description:
Omit for the default `CompetitorSummary` shape - `compact` is an
explicit spelling of that same default. Pass `full` to return the
competitor profile for every row (social links, page URLs) - the
same fields returned alongside `items` by
`GET /competitors/{id}` - plus an `active` boolean so inactive
competitors can be distinguished in the list.

Inactive rows (`active: false`) return the `CompetitorDetail`
shape with the expand-only fields emptied out: `image_icon` is
`null`, and every value inside `social` and `pages` is `null`.
`id`, `name`, `website`, `category`, `created_at`, and `active`
are still populated.

400.description:
Unrecognized query parameter (`unknown_parameter`), or an invalid
value for `active`, `expand`, or `id` (`invalid_parameter`).

get.description:
Full profile for a competitor - metadata, social links, tracked page
URLs - plus per-section item lists for the 12 sections shown on the
in-app Competitor Overview page.

The same lenient "overview" filter the page uses is applied, and rows
recorded while the competitor was inactive are excluded. Items are
not paginated - each section is capped to match what the in-app
overview page renders:

| Section            | Max items |
|--------------------|-----------|
| `blog-posts`       | 3         |
| `press-posts`      | 3         |
| `case-studies`     | 3         |
| `linkedin-posts`   | 3         |
| `x-posts`          | 3         |
| `youtube-videos`   | 3         |
| `events`           | 3         |
| `reviews`          | 3         |
| `job-listings`     | 5         |
| `ads`              | 5         |
| `messaging`        | 5         |
| `metrics-claimed`  | 5         |
| `logos`            | 5         |
| `pricing`          | 1         |

Rows within each section are ordered by `discovered_at` DESC (newest
first).

Sections included: `blog-posts`, `press-posts`, `case-studies`,
`job-listings`, `ads`, `pricing`, `messaging`, `metrics-claimed`, `logos`,
`linkedin-posts`, `x-posts`, `reviews`, `youtube-videos`, `events`.

403 if deactivated, 404 if cross-tenant or unknown.

get.description:
Returns activity across the workspace's active competitors.

Window behaviour depends on `from` / `to`:
  * Omit BOTH `from` and `to` → the complete all-time roster, including items
    that already existed when tracking began (the initial backfill). For
    versioned sections (job-listings, ads, logos, messaging, pricing) this is
    the current live snapshot, not removed history; on this path
    `change_type=added` therefore covers essentially the whole roster and
    `total` is the all-time count.
  * Supply `from` (and/or `to`) → adds / updates / removals in that window only
    (defaults: `from` = 30d ago, `to` = now), excluding backfill.

`sitemap-urls` is the one exception to the backfill rule above: it excludes
`initial_run` items on BOTH paths, so the all-time count for that section
matches what the window path reports rather than including the URLs that were
already present when tracking began.

`sitemap-urls` is also the highest-volume section by a wide margin - a single
crawl can append several hundred URLs for one competitor, and because they are
the most recent rows they land at the front of an unfiltered feed. If you are
after other kinds of change, narrow with `?section=` rather than paging past
them.

To keep list rows lean, the bulky fields `description`, `key_points`,
`pricing_data`, and `excerpt` are OMITTED from each item's `data` here. Fetch
the full payload for a row via `GET /activity/{row_uuid}` or, in batch, via
`GET /activity/items`.

Any `competitor_id` referencing a deactivated competitor yields a 403.

400.description:
Unrecognized query parameter (`unknown_parameter`), or an invalid
parameter value or cursor (`invalid_parameter` / `invalid_cursor`).

get.description:
Look up a single activity row by its UUID. Returns 404 if the row is
unknown, belongs to another workspace, or belongs to an inactive
competitor.

get.description:
Batch sibling of `GET /activity/{row_uuid}` — resolves one-or-more row UUIDs
to their full (untrimmed) payloads in a single request. Use it to drill into
several rows spotted in the lean `GET /activity` list without N round-trips.

Partial success is normal: ids that don't resolve (unknown, in another
workspace, recorded during an inactive period, or malformed) are returned in
`not_found` rather than failing the call. The `data` array order is NOT
guaranteed — match results back to your request by `id`.

parameters.description:
Comma-separated list of activity row UUIDs (max 100, deduped).
Repeating the key (`?id=A&id=B`) is also accepted and merges into
the same list.

BearerAuth.description:
Provision API keys at Settings → API Keys in the meertrack app.
Plaintext is shown once at creation; meertrack stores only a SHA-256
hash of the secret. Lost keys can only be revoked and re-issued.

XRateLimitLimit.description:
Requests allowed per 60-second window, per workspace, per serverless
instance. Aggregate across instances may briefly exceed this - see
the rate-limit notes in the API description.

XRateLimitRemaining.description:
Requests remaining in the current window on the instance that
served this request. Not monotonic across requests (the next
request may land on a different instance with its own counter).

XRateLimitReset.description:
Unix timestamp (seconds) at which the current window resets on
the instance that served this request. Use as the authoritative
backoff signal when paired with a 429.

RowIdPath.name: row_uuid
RowIdPath.description: Activity row UUID, as returned by `GET /activity`.

LimitQuery.name: limit
LimitQuery.description:
Page size. Max 500. Default 100. Use the smallest page that fits
your UI - smaller pages keep `next_cursor` round-trips fast and
cap per-request memory in the API.

Values above 500 are clamped to 500 rather than rejected. A
non-integer value, or anything below 1, yields 400
`invalid_parameter`.

CursorQuery.name: cursor
CursorQuery.description: Opaque cursor from a previous page's `pagination.next_cursor`.

FromQuery.name: from
FromQuery.description: ISO 8601 - inclusive lower bound. On `/activity`, omitting BOTH `from` and `to` returns the full all-time roster (incl. backfill); supplying `from` defaults the window to start 30d ago when only `to` is given.

ToQuery.name: to
ToQuery.description: ISO 8601 - inclusive upper bound. On `/activity`, defaults to now when `from` is supplied. Omitting BOTH `from` and `to` returns the full all-time roster.

CompetitorIdQuery.name: competitor_id
CompetitorIdQuery.description:
Filter to specific competitors. Comma-separated, e.g.
`?competitor_id=A,B`. Repeating the key (`?competitor_id=A&competitor_id=B`)
is also accepted and merges into the same list. Values referencing
deactivated competitors yield 403 `competitor_inactive`; values not in
your workspace yield 403 `forbidden_competitor`.

SectionQuery.name: section
SectionQuery.description:
Filter by section slug(s). Comma-separated, e.g.
`?section=blog-posts,pricing`. Repeating the key is also accepted and
merges into the same list. Unknown slugs yield 400.

ChangeTypeQuery.name: change_type
ChangeTypeQuery.description:
Filter by change type(s). Comma-separated, e.g.
`?change_type=added,updated`. Repeating the key is also accepted and
merges into the same list.

CompetitorIdsQueryDeprecated.name: competitor_ids
CompetitorIdsQueryDeprecated.description: Deprecated alias for `competitor_id`. Supply one spelling or the other, not both.

SectionsQueryDeprecated.name: sections
SectionsQueryDeprecated.description: Deprecated alias for `section`. Supply one spelling or the other, not both.

ChangeTypesQueryDeprecated.name: change_types
ChangeTypesQueryDeprecated.description: Deprecated alias for `change_type`. Supply one spelling or the other, not both.

Unauthorized.description: Missing, malformed, or revoked API key.

error.message: Rate limit of 60 requests per minute exceeded

NotFound.description: Resource not found or belongs to another workspace.

CompetitorInactive.description: Competitor exists but is deactivated in the workspace.

error.message: Competitor is deactivated. Reactivate it in the app to access its data via the API.

ForbiddenCompetitor.description:
Either a `competitor_id` value doesn't belong to your workspace
(`forbidden_competitor`), or it belongs to a deactivated competitor
in your workspace (`competitor_inactive`). Inspect `error.code` to
distinguish - the inactive case can be resolved by reactivating the
competitor in the app.

forbidden_competitor.summary: competitor_id is not in your workspace

error.message: One or more competitor_id values don't belong to your company

competitor_inactive.summary: competitor_id refers to a deactivated competitor

error.message: Competitor "abc-123" is deactivated. Reactivate it in the app to access its data via the API.

InternalError.description: Unexpected server error - safe to retry with backoff.

Pagination.description:
`next_cursor === null` and `has_more === false` always agree (one is
derived from the other server-side). Either field is sufficient to
drive a pagination loop; both are returned so client code can read
whichever fits the idiom better.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor; pass as `?cursor=` to fetch the next page. `null` on the last page.

has_more.description: True iff another page is available. Loop until false. Equivalent to `next_cursor !== null`.

ActivityPagination.description:
Extension of `Pagination` for `/activity`. Adds `total` - the count of
activity rows matching the filters across the requested window. Only
exposed here because the activity feed merges 14 tables in memory, so
the count is computed for free during paging. Don't expect `total` on
other paginated responses.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor; pass as `?cursor=` to fetch the next page. `null` on the last page.

has_more.description: True iff another page is available. Equivalent to `next_cursor !== null`.

total.description:
Total rows matching the filters across the entire window - not
just this page. Stable for the duration of the request; the
underlying data may change between calls so successive pages may
see slightly different totals.

SectionSlug.description:
Public section slug used on `/activity` responses and as the
`section` query parameter on `/activity`. Unknown slugs yield
`400 invalid_parameter`.

SubscriptionTier.description:
Subscription tier. `free_trial` for trials, `paid` for quantity-based
paid subscriptions.

RateLimitSnapshot.description:
Caller's current rate-limit state on the instance that served this
request. Same caveats as the `X-RateLimit-*` headers - values are
per-instance, not workspace-global.

auth_type.description:
How this request authenticated. `api_key` callers also get a
populated `key` block below; `oauth` callers have no API-key
record, so `key` is `null`.

subject.description:
Stable caller identifier used for rate limiting and auditing —
the Supabase `sub` claim for OAuth callers, the workspace id for
`mt_live_` API-key callers.

key.description: `null` for OAuth callers, which have no API-key record.

CompetitorDetail.description:
Full competitor profile as returned by `GET /competitors?expand=full`
and as the profile block on `GET /competitors/{id}` (minus the
`active` boolean, which is always true on the single-competitor
endpoint since inactive competitors 403). The bulk list can include
deactivated competitors, so consumers need a way to distinguish
them.

CompetitorOverviewItems.description:
Per-section item lists for the overview page. Keys are section slugs;
values are arrays of `SectionItem` (see the `SectionItem` union for
the per-section shape). All 14 keys are always present; empty
sections are returned as `[]`.

competitor.description:
Competitor display name. Carried on every section item for
symmetry with the file-export format used by the in-app CSV
and JSON exports - so the same DTO can be flattened to a row
without joining against a separate competitor table.

On `/activity` and `/activity/{row_uuid}` responses this name
is **redundant** with the envelope's `competitor.name`; the
envelope additionally carries the competitor `id`. When you
need to key by competitor in those responses, use the
envelope. The duplicate is preserved for export-shape
compatibility and won't be removed in `v1`.

added_at.description: Most recent time the listing was observed appearing on the page (snapshot+event).

removed_at.description: Most recent time the listing was observed disappearing from the page.

AdItem.description:
Competitor advertisement (Google or LinkedIn). Snapshot table keyed off
add/remove events - same access pattern as `JobListingItem`. Ads have no
title; `content` is the ad copy (present on LinkedIn ads, absent on
image-only Google ads), `image_url` is the creative (or a video thumbnail
when `ad_format` is `VIDEO`), and `ad_url` is the ad's landing URL when
available (present on Google ads, `null` otherwise).

ad_url.description: The ad's landing URL when available (Google ads); `null` otherwise.

added_at.description: Most recent time the ad was observed running.

removed_at.description: Most recent time the ad was observed no longer running.

pricing_data.description:
Opaque JSON payload - the scraped pricing tiers and structure
as the parser saw them. Shape is not stable across competitors
or releases; treat as untyped JSON unless you've inspected
samples for the specific competitor.

XPostItem.description:
X (formerly Twitter) post. Stored append-only, keyed off `posted_date` -
same access pattern as `LinkedInPostItem`. Unlike LinkedIn, X posts
persist `url` and `post_id` separately in the source table, so both
are returned as-is rather than rewriting one from the other.

name.description: Account display name on X (the post author's handle/profile name).

rating.description: Free-text rating, e.g. `"5/5"` or `"4 out of 5"`. Not normalized.

sentiment.description: Free-text sentiment label, e.g. `"positive"`, `"negative"`, `"mixed"`. Not an enum.

SitemapUrlItem.description:
Append-only feed of newly-discovered URLs in the competitor's
sitemap. Useful for catching pages that haven't surfaced anywhere
else yet (new product launches, hidden landing pages, lifecycle
changes). On its own, a row only tells you a URL appeared - pair
with the corresponding section feed for content.

Because the feed is append-only, `change_type` is always `added`
and `change_date` always equals `discovered_at` (the date the URL
was first seen). URLs that have since started returning 404 are
excluded.

This is a high-volume section - a single crawl can add several
hundred URLs for one competitor, which will dominate the front of
an unfiltered `/activity` feed. Use `?section=` to include or
exclude it deliberately.

SectionItem.description:
Union of all section item shapes. The branch is selected by the
envelope's `section` value (path param on the per-section endpoint;
the `section` field on `ActivityItem` / `ActivityDetailResponse`),
not by inspecting properties - there is no in-payload discriminator,
because several branches overlap on `title`/`url`/`posted_date`.

Mapping: `blog-posts` → `BlogPostItem`, `press-posts` →
`PressPostItem`, `case-studies` → `CaseStudyItem`, `job-listings` →
`JobListingItem`, `ads` → `AdItem`, `pricing` → `PricingItem`,
`linkedin-posts` → `LinkedInPostItem`, `x-posts` → `XPostItem`,
`reviews` → `ReviewItem`, `youtube-videos` → `YouTubeVideoItem`,
`events` → `EventItem`, `messaging` → `MessagingItem`,
`metrics-claimed` → `MetricsClaimedItem`, `logos` → `LogoItem`,
`sitemap-urls` → `SitemapUrlItem`.

`PressPostItem` and `CaseStudyItem` are intentionally identical to
`BlogPostItem` today and so are not included as separate branches
(validators would treat the union as ambiguous). Use the `section`
envelope value to know which branch you got.

not_found.description: Requested ids that did not resolve (unknown, cross-workspace, inactive, or malformed).

DigestSummary.description:
LLM-generated summary payload. The shape documented here is the
target - older digests may omit `themes` entirely, and the LLM
occasionally adds new top-level keys ahead of a corresponding
spec bump (which is why `additionalProperties` is permissive).
Treat unrecognized keys as opaque and don't fail validation on
them; we'll bump the schema and `info.version` when we promise a
new key as stable.

summary.description:
LLM-generated summary. Newer digests are objects shaped like
`DigestSummary`; older digests may be plain strings; either may
be `null`. Treat as opaque unless you've verified the shape.
